title: Hindu group warns of protest against Ramayana 2

ai.summary: The Hindu Janajagruti Samiti (HJS) warns of nationwide protests against potential distortions in the sequel to Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, claiming the film misrepresents Hindu religious figures and events from Valmiki's epic.

facts.claim: The Hindu Janajagruti Samiti (HJS) has raised objections to Nitesh Tiwari’s recently released film Ramayana: Rise of a Legend
facts.quote: The Hindu Janajagruti Samiti (HJS) has raised objections to Nitesh Tiwari’s recently released film Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, alleging that it distorts Maharshi Valmiki’s epic and hurts Hindu religious sentiments.

facts.claim: HJS has appealed to Hindus to boycott the film and warned of nationwide protests if similar alleged distortions appear in its second part
facts.quote: The organisation has appealed to Hindus to boycott the film and warned of nationwide protests if similar alleged distortions appear in its second part.

facts.claim: HJS Goa coordinator Manoj Solanki alleged that several scenes misrepresent the characters of Lord Ram, Sita, Lakshman and Ravana
facts.quote: In a statement issued on Tuesday, HJS Goa coordinator Manoj Solanki alleged that several scenes misrepresent the characters of Lord Ram, Sita, Lakshman and Ravana.

facts.claim: The organisation particularly objected to Ravana’s portrayal as a ruler who protects the oppressed and women’s dignity, claiming it glorifies the demon king while overlooking his traditional depiction in the epic
facts.quote: The organisation particularly objected to Ravana’s portrayal as a ruler who protects the oppressed and women’s dignity, claiming it glorifies the demon king while overlooking his traditional depiction in the epic.

facts.claim: It also criticised the Shurpanakha episode, alleging that the film introduces scenes in which Sita reprimands Lakshman for disfiguring a woman and Lord Ram apologises to demons Khara and Dushana
facts.quote: It also criticised the Shurpanakha episode, alleging that the film introduces scenes in which Sita reprimands Lakshman for disfiguring a woman and Lord Ram apologises to demons Khara and Dushana.

facts.claim: HJS claimed these incidents contradict the original Valmiki Ramayana
facts.quote: HJS claimed these incidents contradict the original Valmiki Ramayana.

facts.claim: The organisation further alleged that Lord Ram and Lakshman are shown retreating during battles, while Lakshman is portrayed as arrogant, short-tempered and disrespectful towards sages
facts.quote: The organisation further alleged that Lord Ram and Lakshman are shown retreating during battles, while Lakshman is portrayed as arrogant, short-tempered and disrespectful towards sages.

facts.claim: It also questioned the film’s depiction of Sita’s response during Ravana’s abduction
facts.quote: It also questioned the film’s depiction of Sita’s response during Ravana’s abduction.

facts.claim: HJS accused the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) of failing to adequately examine the religious aspects of the film
facts.quote: HJS accused the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) of failing to adequately examine the religious aspects of the film.

facts.claim: It urged the board to consult religious scholars before approving movies based on sacred epics
facts.quote: It urged the board to consult religious scholars before approving movies based on sacred epics.

facts.claim: Solanki appealed to the filmmakers to screen the second part before Hindu religious leaders, seers and Ramayana scholars ahead of its release
facts.quote: Solanki appealed to the filmmakers to screen the second part before Hindu religious leaders, seers and Ramayana scholars ahead of its release.

facts.claim: He also urged the government to take note of the objections
facts.quote: He also urged the government to take note of the objections.

facts.claim: Warning of further action, Solanki said the organisation would launch protests across the country if similar alleged distortions appear in the sequel
facts.quote: Warning of further action, Solanki said the organisation would launch protests across the country if similar alleged distortions appear in the sequel.
